title: The hotel behind The Shining

slides.text: THIS HOTEL GAVE STEPHEN KING THE SHINING
Estes Park, Colorado. The Stanley Hotel opened in 1909, high in the Rocky Mountains.
It was built by F.O. Stanley, co-inventor of the Stanley Steamer car.
October 1974. Stephen King and his wife check in... the night before the hotel shuts down for winter.
They were almost the only guests. Empty halls. Chairs stacked on tables. They stayed in Room 217.
King said he had a nightmare that night about his young son being chased through the halls.
By morning, he had the idea for The Shining.
For decades staff and guests have reported strange things: footsteps, voices, a piano playing by itself.
Room 217 is now one of the most requested rooms in the hotel. You can book it tonight.
